Water temperature, discharge, and water level for ~300 BC hydrometric
stations, queryable straight from S3 — no database, nothing to download up
front. A [monthly GitHub Actions cron](.github/workflows/snapshot.yml)
re-pulls the full ~18-month window Environment Canada (ECCC) serves and
compacts it into one deduplicated parquet dataset, so QC corrections
automatically replace earlier provisional readings and the record keeps
growing month over month. The same dataset carries the archive from before
the cron began: water temperature back to 2002, daily discharge to 2016.

<br>

## Quick start

```r
install.packages(c("arrow", "dplyr", "duckdb", "dbplyr", "lubridate"))

source("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NewGraphEnvironment/water-temp-bc/main/scripts/query-helpers.R")

# water temperature, one station, last 6 months
query_canonical(parameter = 5, stations = "07EA004", from = Sys.Date() - 180) |>
  dplyr::collect()
```

`query_canonical()` returns a lazy dplyr query — filter by `parameter`,
`stations`, `from`/`to`, chain any dplyr verbs, and `collect()` when you want
the data in memory. Typical queries return in a few seconds. No AWS account
or credentials needed — the bucket is fully public.
[`scripts/query.R`](scripts/query.R) has more worked examples (daily means
across stations, latest reading per station).

<br>

## What's in it

| `Parameter` | Name | Unit | From | Rows | Stations |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `5` | Water temperature | °C | 2002-04 | 17,292,881 | 306 |
| `6` | Discharge (daily mean) | m³/s | 2015-12 | 571,092 | 264 |
| `46` | Water level (primary sensor) | m | 2022-06 | 101,763,401 | 299 |
| `47` | Discharge (primary sensor derived) | m³/s | 2022-06 | 91,806,298 | 262 |
| `1` | Air temperature | °C | 2022-06 → 2024-01 only | 463,749 | 15 |
| `18` | Precipitation | mm | 2022-06 → 2024-01 only | 301,487 | 9 |

Counts as of the 2026-09 compaction. **For realtime discharge use `47`, not
`6`**: `6` is one value per day, while `5`, `46` and `47` are high-frequency
sensor readings. Everything grows monthly except `1` and `18`, which came
from one 2022–2024 pull and are frozen. With no `from`, `query_canonical()`
returns the whole record, so filter by date when you want recent data only.
Station locations and metadata live in `stations_realtime.parquet` (table
below).

<br>

## Data layout

```
s3://water-temp-bc/data/
├── canonical/Parameter=<n>/part-*.parquet     # THE dataset — query this
├── realtime/<yyyy>/<mm>/snapshot_.../         # raw monthly pulls (provenance only)
├── historic/realtime_raw_*.parquet            # frozen originals of the pre-2024-10 archive
├── historic/normalized/*.parquet              # the same, normalized; already merged into canonical/
└── stations_realtime.parquet                  # station metadata
```

- `canonical/` is deduplicated at build time — newest QC'd value per
  station, parameter, and timestamp. `query_canonical()` and
  `arrow::open_dataset()` both read it directly.
- `realtime/` keeps every raw overlapping pull; ~2/3 duplicate rows by
  design. Only useful if you need pre-correction history.
- `historic/` holds four files pulled between 2022 and 2025, before the
  monthly cron existed. They overlap each other and have mismatched
  schemas; you don't need them, because `canonical/` already contains
  their deduplicated content ([#19](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/water-temp-bc/issues/19)).
- Single files fetched by URL need the region, e.g.
  `https://water-temp-bc.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/data/realtime/2026/06/snapshot_2026-06-01/chunk_001.parquet`
  (note: files under `canonical/` carry `Parameter` in the directory name,
  not as a column). The store is rewritten ~12:00–14:00 UTC on the 1st of
  each month.

<br>

### The record before 2024-10

Rows dated before the first monthly pull come from the historic files, and
they carry older vocabularies. Details are in
[`research/historic-archive.md`](research/historic-archive.md).

- **`Approval`**: rows from ECCC's bulk dump (water temperature 2002–2022,
  daily discharge 2015-12 → 2022-12) carry ECCC's codes `1`, `2` or `4`,
  not `Provisional/Provisoire` / `Final/Finales`. Some 2022–2025 rows have
  no `Approval` or `Grade` because the pull that carried them had dropped
  those columns.
- **`Symbol`**: only daily discharge from the bulk dump (2015-12 → 2022-12)
  has flags, in ECCC's own codes (`ICE`, `ES`, `E`, `PX`, …). No other
  row, current feed included, carries a `B` (ice) or `E` (estimate) flag,
  so a missing flag does not mean open water.
- **`harvested_at`** on these rows is the last `Date` in the file they came
  from, a lower bound on when it was pulled.

```r
# daily discharge at Bulkley River near Houston, 2016 onward
query_canonical(parameter = 6, stations = "08EE003", from = as.Date("2016-01-01")) |>
  dplyr::select(Date, Value, Approval, Symbol) |>
  dplyr::collect()
```

`r if (params$rmd_on == FALSE) "Please see http://www.newgraphenvironment.com/water-temp-bc for the published table of station details and a sample query."`

```{r q-stations, eval = TRUE}
# Station metadata (location, drainage, timezone, etc.) — unchanged file path,
# managed separately from the realtime snapshots.
stations <- arrow::read_parquet("s3://water-temp-bc/data/stations_realtime.parquet")
```

```{r q-range, eval = params$update_query}
# Per-station date ranges in the canonical dataset. Cached locally; refresh
# on demand with params$update_query (seconds against canonical/).
range <- query_canonical(parameter = 5) |>
  dplyr::group_by(STATION_NUMBER) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    min_date = min(Date, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_date = max(Date, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::collect()

saveRDS(range, "data/result.rds")
```

```{r stations-cap, echo=FALSE, results="asis", eval=identical(params$rmd_on, TRUE)}
my_caption <- "Realtime station information with the date range of water temperature data available in s3://water-temp-bc/data/canonical/."
my_tab_caption_rmd()
```

```{r tab-stations, echo=FALSE, eval=identical(params$rmd_on, TRUE)}
range <- readRDS("data/result.rds")

dplyr::left_join(
  stations,
  range,
  by = "STATION_NUMBER"
  ) |>
  my_dt_table(cols_freeze_left = 2, escape = FALSE)
```

<br>

### Sample query

The chunk below pulls the last 6 months of water-temperature observations
for one station via `query_canonical()`. It's the same pattern as Example 1
in `scripts/query.R`.

```{r q-sample, eval = TRUE}
sample <- query_canonical(
  parameter = 5,
  stations  = "07EA004",
  from      = Sys.Date() - 180
) |>
  dplyr::select(STATION_NUMBER, Date, Value, Unit, Grade, Approval) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Date) |>
  dplyr::collect()
```

```{r sample-cap, echo=FALSE, results="asis", eval=identical(params$rmd_on, TRUE)}
my_caption <- "Last 6 months of water temperature (Parameter == 5) for station 07EA004, pulled via query_canonical() from s3://water-temp-bc/data/canonical/."
my_tab_caption_rmd()
```

```{r tab-sample, echo=FALSE, eval=identical(params$rmd_on, TRUE)}
sample |>
  my_dt_table(cols_freeze_left = 2, escape = FALSE)
```
